title: Fabrication of the Composite Regenerative Peripheral Nerve Interface (C-RPNI) in the Adult Rat
protocol: Anesthetize donor rat in an induction chamber utilizing a solution of 5% isoflurane in oxygen at 0.8-1 L/min.
Remove the anesthetized rat from the induction chamber and place on a rebreathing nose cone, lowering the isoflurane to 2-2.5% for maintenance of anesthesia.
Administer a solution of 0.02-0.03 mL Carprofen (50 mg/mL) in 0.2 mL of sterile saline subcutaneously between the shoulder blades for analgesia.
Apply artificial tears ointment to both eyes to prevent corneal ulcers.
Shave the entire lower hindlimb(s), ankle region, and sides of paw(s) using clippers.
Cleanse chosen hindlimb and plantar surface of paw with alcohol.
Follow cleansing with iodopovidone solution.
End cleanse by applying a final cleanse with alcohol to remove residual iodopovidone.
Burr the plantar surface of the paw using a hand-held micro motor high speed drill at 4000 rpm with a fine grit polishing stone.
Apply drips of saline while burring to prevent skin burning.
Remove the epidermis until the underlying dermis has a shiny appearance and shows pinpoint bleeding.
Apply a tourniquet to the lower extremity to slow blood flow.
Sharp excision of plantar skin using a #15 scalpel.
Place removed skin in saline-moistened gauze to prevent desiccation.
Repeat steps 1.5-1.9 if performing two constructs.
Under a microscope at 20x magnification, use micro-scissors to remove tendinous and connective tissue from the deep layer of the skin graft.
Take care not to create holes in the graft during removal.
The thinned dermal graft should be slightly opaque, containing only dermis, measuring approximately 0.5 cm x 1.0cm in size.
Place the prepared graft in saline-moistened gauze until ready for C-RPNI construct fabrication.
Utilize the graft within 2 hours of harvest.
Make a longitudinal incision along the anterior aspect of the lower hindlimb from just above the ankle to just below the knee using a #15 scalpel.
Dissect through subcutaneous tissue to expose the underlying musculature.
At the distal aspect of the incision, expose the tendinous insertions of the lower limb musculature.
Isolate the distal EDL tendon from other tendons in the area without incising its insertion.
Insert both tines of a forceps underneath the tendon and exert upward pressure to cause tendon excursion.
Perform a distal tenotomy with sharp iris scissors.
Separate the muscle from surrounding tissues bluntly with tenotomies working proximally to find the tendinous origin.
Once the proximal tendon is visualized, perform a tenotomy utilizing sharp iris scissors.
Place the muscle graft in saline-moistened gauze to prevent desiccation.
Euthanize donor rat primarily by intra-cardiac KCl injection followed by secondary euthanasia with bilateral puncture pneumothorax.
Shave the desired thigh and cleanse with alcohol.
Cleanse the shaved area with betadine.
End cleansing with alcohol to remove traces of betadine.
Move the animal from the surgical prep table to the surgical microscope table.
Place the animal on a heating pad with a temperature probe for body temperature maintenance.
Maintain isoflurane at 2-2.5% and oxygen at 0.8-1 L/min.
Mark the incision extending from just distal to the sciatic notch to the inferior portion of the knee.
Make the incision with a #15 blade, cutting through the underlying biceps femoris fascia.
Carefully dissect through the biceps femoris muscle using either a hemostat or blunt-tipped micro-scissors to reach the space under the muscle.
Identify the common peroneal (CP) nerve among the three branches of the sciatic nerve.
Isolate the CP nerve from other sciatic branches using fine-tipped forceps and micro-scissors.
Carefully remove any lingering connective tissue distally around the isolated CP nerve.
Sharply transect the CP nerve at the point where it crosses the surface of the knee with a pair of sharp micro-scissors.
Carefully free connective tissue from the CP nerve.
Work proximally to free 2 cm of the CP nerve.
Remove central tendinous tissue and a small segment of epimysium from the muscle graft.
Secure the epineurium of the transected CP nerve end to the muscle graft with two interrupted stitches using an 8-0 nylon suture.
Secure the muscle graft to the femur periosteum proximally and distally with single 6-0 nylon interrupted stitches.
Place an 8-0 nylon stitch at the inferior, central margin of the muscle graft epimysium to secure it to the CP nerve epineurium.
Remove the skin graft from the saline-moistened gauze.
Arrange the skin graft on the muscle graft to cover the nerve and most of the muscle.
Ensure the deep margin of the dermis rests on the muscle.
Trim any excess dermis extending beyond the muscle border.
Secure the skin graft to the muscle graft using 8-0 nylon interrupted sutures (4-8 total).
Close the biceps femoris fascia over the construct with a running suture using 5-0 chromic suture.
Close the overlying skin with a running suture using 4-0 chromic suture.
Swab the surgical area with an alcohol pad.
Apply antibiotic ointment to the surgical site.
